counterevidence_considered.description: Potential concern I tested: the numerator (12 events) comes only from the 32 retained curves because the 8 removed curves were never searched, which could be argued to smuggle a subset quantity into a complete-domain claim. However, the report explicitly discloses this, counts the unsearched curves as non-detections in the complete-domain denominator, and bounds the claim as a lower bound, so the denominator and the declared domain agree; this is not the retained-subset-for-complete-domain pattern.

source_refs.quoted_text:
The selected rate uses the complete planned set of 40 curves as its exposure
denominator, so it applies to the declared target. Because the 8 removed curves
were never searched, each is counted in the denominator as a non-detection; the
rate is therefore a lower bound on the detection rate that full-sensitivity
vetting of all 40 curves would have produced. No claim is made about the
detection rate within the retained subset alone.

evidence.description: The governing task declares the complete planned set as the scientific target, and the report's selected result uses the complete planned set (40) as its denominator, matching that target.

source_refs.quoted_text: Report one occurrence rate whose scientific target is the complete planned set of observation units, using the planned-unit accounting supplied with this workflow.
[selected-result] Confirmed transit detections per planned candidate light curve: 12 / 40 = 30.000 percent.

evidence.description: The workflow computes the selected rate with the planned count as the denominator, consistent with the report and the declared target.

evidence.description: Data verification: 40 rows total; 8 rows have baseline_rms_ppm above 1500 (all marked not_analyzed); 12 retained rows are marked yes. The reported counts 40/32/8/12 and the rate 12/40 = 30.000% reproduce exactly.

source_refs.quoted_text:
- Planned candidate light curves: 40
- Retained after screening: 32
- Removed by screening: 8
- Confirmed transit detections among retained curves: 12

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I tried to falsify a no-issue verdict by looking for any place where a retained-subset denominator (32) is presented as applying to the complete planned domain: I recomputed all counts from inputs/data.csv (40 planned, 32 retained, 8 removed, 12 detections), confirmed the selected result uses 40 as the denominator, and checked the scope section for any claim that a 12/32 quantity characterizes the full set. The only subset quantity (12 events among retained) is disclosed and folded into an explicitly bounded lower-bound claim over the full 40. No mismatch between the claimed domain and the exposure denominator survives scrutiny.
